narration:
The mountain train stops in the deep, crunchy snow. Steam puffs into the cold air. Old Howard Roundtail's briefcase is gone! Inside is his grandma's sketchbook. Foxes, wolves, bears and bunnies all look at each other. Can you find the truth?

Tip: type "notebook" (or "n") to open your case notebook. It holds what you know, who you have met, and every clue you have found. Type "help" to see what else you can do.

Crisp snow crunches under your boots. The mountain train puffs warm steam. A big red clock ticks above you. A wooden fence runs along the platform. A door says Post Room.

Howard hurries over, patting his empty paws. "Oh, you came! Thank goodness."

Mabel checks her big brass watch. She nods down the platform, twice.
Warm steam puffs past you. The red clock ticks. Maybe the post room or the fence has more to find.
You step into the cozy post room. Six open crates, stuffed with letters. Every lid has Mabel's tick mark on it.
You kneel by the wooden fence. Tiny curls of snow-dusted wood sit nearby. Pencil shavings in the snow by the fence. Someone sat drawing here for ages.

Crisp snow crunches under your boots. A giant paper Star Lantern glows in the middle of the square. Snowy cottages ring the edges. A notice board and a snowy bench wait nearby.

A small snow fox kit bounces over. Her pink mittens are too big. A pencil peeks from behind one ear.

"Are you a real detective? I've never met one! Want to see my drawings?"
Tansy sits on the snowy bench, sketching the big Star Lantern. Her pink mittens are too big. She waves at you with her pencil. "Oh! A real detective! Want to see my drawings?"
"I drew everyone who got off the train! Nobody had a brown case. Just Rufus's crates, Wanda's box, Bruno's cart and Sylvie's basket."

narration: Tansy shuts her sketchbook with a snap. "Thanks for chatting! I must draw the Star Lantern now." She waves her big pink mittens. You stay in the Village Square, ready to look around.

Warm wooden walls wrap around you. Red seats line the carriage. Frosty windows glow with soft lantern light.

You can look at Howard's seat, the luggage rack, the seat across the aisle, or the little stove.

A tall, thin red fox in a navy jacket stands nearby. He twists a brass button. He stares at nothing in particular. "Don't mind me," he mutters.
You glance up over the seat. A new paper star lantern hangs above Howard's seat. Its glue is still sticky.
You look up at the luggage rack. A paper tag hangs on one empty spot. An empty rack just behind Howard's seat. Its tag says: Wanda Greycoat, sled box.
Snow glows on the frosty windows. Rufus leans by the warm stove, arms folded. He eyes you carefully. "Oh. It's you. Go on, then. Ask away."
Rufus jumps and tugs his cap. "Me? No! I was in the luggage car. Then the post room. Honest!"

narration: Rufus gives a quick nod. "Right. Back to work, then. Bye!" He tugs his cap and smiles a little. You stay where you are. The little stove glows warm. Frost sparkles on the windows. Time to look around.
You bend down and look closely. Red fox hairs on the seat across the aisle. The cushion is squashed flat.
You warm your hands by the little stove. It feels cozy. Nothing is hidden here. Maybe the back door has more to tell.
You push the back door open. Cold air puffs in. Big wolf pawprints in the snow, going down the back steps of the carriage.

Crisp snow crunches under your boots. You step into a cozy log tea house. A fire crackles. Honey jars shine on the honey counter. Nearby, the fireside tables wait for guests.

Bruno, a big round bear in a striped blue apron, waves a flour-dusted paw. "Welcome! Cocoa? Coming right up!"

Wanda, a tall grey wolf in a red woolly hat, stands by the fire. She looks away quickly. "Hello," she says softly.
Wanda sits by the warm fire, hugging her cup. She looks up, then quickly away. "Hello," she says softly. "I didn't do anything wrong, you know."
Wanda holds her cup tighter. "I don't know about any paw marks," she says softly. "I got my box from the front of the train."
